description: F-CORE-035 meets F-CORE-042: a rule that REFUSES a posting has to be readable, or the refusal cannot be explained from inside the library. A screen with an account picker can only learn which combinations are forbidden by trying them and reading the error — the same argument that made `tenantConfiguration` report `dimensionRules` in the first place. Two things are pinned here that were pinned nowhere else. FIRST, `accountCombinationRules` appears in `tenantConfiguration` at all: `core/tenant-configuration` covers the first predicate and stops there, and the only place the second one was ever read back was a fixture on the SHIPPED German pack — which meant the German pack could not declare another rule without the readability claim going red (that fixture is now `de-entgeltminderung-erzwungen-current`, and this one carries what it gave up). Pinning the whole list is legitimate HERE and was not there, and the difference is the whole point of the superseded register: this pack is the fixture's own data, so the list cannot move underneath it. SECOND, two constraint modules ADD UP rather than replace — `pack-library/CLAUDE.md` says so and nothing held it: both modules' rules are in force at once, both fire, and both are reported. Order in the reported list follows resolution, which is byte-equal in both languages; that it is stable is worth pinning, that it means anything is not — a pack author must not read priority into it, because the predicates are independent and every rule is checked.

expect.comment: Module B is in force at the same time and in the same tenant. Adding a second constraint module did not replace the first — which is what `several constraint modules add up` means, and until now nothing checked it.
Neither rule is triggered, so nothing fires.
Both modules' rules, read back through one projection. A caller can render the prohibition BEFORE the user posts instead of translating an exit code afterwards.
